meta.title: Well Profiler App for the Open .well Format
meta.description: Welldot (formerly Well Profiler) is a free well profiler app for well profiles — visualize, edit, and export in the open, versioned .well format.
featureList: Create, visualize, and export geological and construction well profiles
Pump installation history and general attachments (.well v2.3)

editorMeta.title: Well Profile Editor
editorMeta.description: Free browser-based well profiler app to create, visualize, and export geological and construction well profiles as open, versioned .well files.

hero.body: Free editor to create, visualize, and export geological and construction profiles. A simple JSON, versioned, readable by any language.

format.intro: Today, well data lives in PDFs that don't talk to each other. The {well} file is a simple, versioned format to change that — a single JSON that fully describes a well, from construction and geology to pump tests, installed pumps and maintenance history, designed as an {standard}.

props.title: Visualization
props.body: Free D3.js library to render and export geological and construction profiles at real scale.

props.title: Record
props.body: Predictable structure to archive and version well data, ready for submission and auditing.

props.title: Research
props.body: Organized metric fields allow cross-referencing and comparing wells across aquifers, regions, and eras.

props.title: Open
props.body: Human-readable JSON, public specification, and permissive license — free to use, extend, and contribute.

props.title: Pump tests
props.body: Hydrodynamic events and derived aquifer parameters — transmissivity, storativity, specific capacity — recorded as structured time series.

props.title: Operation & history
props.body: Pump installations with nameplate, intake depth, riser and electrical data, typed documents, and a dated log of maintenance and incidents that follows the well through its working life.

intention.body: Today, a water well's data exists in many places: in the driller's notebook, in the consultant's spreadsheet, in the PDF report submitted to the licensing authority. Each in its own format, each {unreadable}. {welldot} and the {well} format were created to solve this.
intention.originNote: This project began as {wellProfiler}, a tool to draw well diagrams. It's growing into something broader: an open platform for the entire lifecycle of well data — not just the drawing.

pillars.title: Live editor
pillars.body: Tables linked to the drawing. Edit a layer, see the profile redrawn at real scale.

pillars.title: Open format
pillars.body: Human-readable JSON, public specification, and Apache 2.0 license. Implement in any language.

pillars.title: Submission-ready
pillars.body: A4 PDFs at real scale, with header, metadata, and multi-page drawing.

contexts.text1: A single human-readable text file: archivable in folders, versionable in git, indexable in databases, {aiEm}. The core is strict where it matters — {si}, {wgs}, English keys — and {flexible} everywhere else.
contexts.text2: The repository includes a ready-made {skill}: point any agent to {repo} and it operates the format natively.

horizon.intro: v2.3 covers geological, construction, and hydrodynamic profiles — pump tests, aquifer analysis, pump installations, water-use permits and their conditions, general attachments, and operational history. The specification evolves openly to embrace what's still ahead.

props.title: Native .las
props.body: Import and storage of LAS geophysical profiles, side by side with the lithological profile.

props.title: Water quality
props.body: Physical-chemical and bacteriological analyses linked to sampling, depth, and date.

props.title: Production & operation
props.body: Meters, produced volumes checked against permit limits, and operating regime — the next operational blocks.

props.title: Community extensions
props.body: Namespaces for fields specific to agencies and regions, without breaking the standardized core.

tools.intro: welldot is a set of small, independent packages. Use the editor, or pull just the piece you need into your own stack.

cards.title: \@welldot/core
cards.body: Types, Zod validators, and serialization utilities for the .well format — the foundation everything else builds on.

cards.title: \@welldot/utils
cards.body: Profile analysis utilities: depth calculations, cylindrical volumes, and gravel pack volume estimates.

cards.title: \@welldot/render
cards.body: The D3-based SVG renderer that draws every profile on this site — embeddable in any web app.

cards.title: Profiler app
cards.body: This editor, source and all. Nuxt 4 + Vue 3, deployed at welldot.org — fork it or read how it's built.

cta.subtitle: Free to use. Free to implement. Open forever.

aiImporter.title: AI Import
aiImporter.description: The AI Import will turn a well report — PDF, image, or document — into a .well profile automatically. It isn't available yet.

boreHole.title: Bore Hole
boreHole.drillingMethodInfo: Drilling method used to open this bore hole interval. Pick one of the suggestions — rotary, percussion, cable tool, auger or air hammer.
boreHole.drillingMethodFreeText: This field is free text: if the method is not in the list, just type it (e.g. reverse circulation, sonic, jetting) and it will be saved as-is.

wellCase.title: Casing
wellCase.typeInfo: Material of the casing that lines the well and holds the bore hole walls, e.g. PVC, geomechanical PVC, carbon steel or stainless steel.
wellCase.typeFreeText: This field is free text: if the material is not in the list, just type it (e.g. HDPE, blank steel pipe) and it will be saved as-is.

reduction.title: Reduction
reduction.typeInfo: Material or shape of the reducer that connects the two diameters, e.g. PVC, geomechanical PVC, carbon steel, conical or stepped.
reduction.typeFreeText: This field is free text: if the material is not in the list, just type it (e.g. conical, stepped) and it will be saved as-is.

centralizer.title: Centralizers
centralizer.typeInfo: Kind or material of the centralizers clamped to the casing to keep it centered in the bore hole, e.g. spring bow, rigid, polymer, carbon steel or stainless steel.
centralizer.typeFreeText: This field is free text: if the type or material is not in the list, just type it and it will be saved as-is.
centralizer.descriptionInfo: Optional notes about these centralizers, such as manufacturer, model, material or how they were installed.
centralizer.hint: One row per interval. Use the same depth in From and To for a single centralizer; leave spacing empty if unknown.

wellScreen.title: Screen
wellScreen.typeInfo: Material (or construction) of the screen that lets water into the well, e.g. PVC, geomechanical PVC, carbon steel or stainless steel.
wellScreen.typeFreeText: This field is free text: if the material is not in the list, just type it (e.g. wire wound stainless steel, bridge slot) and it will be saved as-is.

holeFill.title: Hole Fill
holeFill.typeInfo: Role of the material in the annular space between casing and bore hole wall: gravel pack is the filter gravel around the screens; seal is the cement or bentonite that isolates the annulus against contamination.
holeFill.descriptionInfo: Material actually used in this interval, e.g. grain size of the gravel (1–2 mm quartz gravel) or seal material (cement grout, bentonite pellets).

general.name: Well Name
general.wellTypeInfo: Indicates the type of structure the well is, according to its construction (e.g. tubular, hand dug, horizontal, infiltration gallery). It is not the drilling method, nor what the well is used for: use Well Purpose for that. Artesian is a hydraulic condition, detected from the water levels.

artesianDeprecated.message: "Artesian" is deprecated as a well type since .well v2.1 — it is a hydraulic condition, not a construction method. Pick the construction method instead; a flowing artesian condition is recorded as a negative static level in the hydrodynamic events.

general.flowingArtesian: Flowing artesian — latest static level is above ground
general.clickOrDragPin: Click the map or drag the pin

wellIds.title: Well Identifiers
wellIds.primaryTooltip: Primary identifier — the canonical ID for this well

info.label: About well identifiers
info.title: What are well identifiers?
info.what: Other codes this same well has in external databases and registries. They make the .well file compatible with those systems, so the well can be cross-referenced and matched across different sources.
info.exampleGrant: Water-use permit (outorga) number issued by the water resources agency
info.exampleCompany: An internal code used by a company, utility or driller
info.fields: Authority is the name of the registry or institution that issued the code (pick a suggestion or type your own). ID is the code exactly as issued; keep leading zeros and separators (e.g. SP-0042819).
info.primary: Use the radio button to mark the main identifier. If none is marked, the first one is treated as the main one. Each authority + ID pair must be unique.

general.attachmentsInfo: Files about the well as a whole, such as the drilling report or an as-built drawing. Attachments of pumps, tests and history entries stay on their own records.

fields.author: Author
fields.eventInfo: Event holding the data produced by this task, e.g. the level measured or the pumping test performed.
fields.statusInfo: The latest status change sets the current status of the well.

events.title: Hydrodynamic Events
events.comingSoon: Full editing available in the Hydrodynamic tab

hydrodynamicEvents.title: Hydrodynamic Events
hydrodynamicEvents.ledgerNote: Chronological ledger — new records are appended, not overwritten.

analyses.inDevBody: The Analyses tab will allow entering aquifer test results (transmissivity, specific capacity, storage coefficient).

hydrodynamicEvents.retractedInfo: A later event corrects this one. It stays in the file but no longer counts.
hydrodynamicEvents.correctionInfo: This event corrects an earlier one.

attachments.documentTypeInfo: What the document is (.well v2.3). Optional — leave empty when unsure.

pump.title: Pump installations
pump.intro: One entry per installation. A pump pulled and reinstalled gets a new entry with the same serial number. The current pump is the one without a removal date.
pump.submergenceInfo: Intake depth minus the latest dynamic level.
pump.submergenceNegative: The intake is above the latest dynamic level.

fields.typeInfo: Solar is a power source, not a pump type. Free text is allowed.
fields.removedAtInfo: Leave empty while the pump is installed.
fields.serialInfo: Links reinstallations of the same unit.
fields.intakeDepthInfo: Depth of the pump intake from ground level. The profile draws the pump ending here.
fields.ratedPowerInfo: Stored in kW; shown in the unit chosen in Settings. 1 cv = 0.7355 kW · 1 hp = 0.7457 kW.
fields.riserDiameterInfo: As-built outer diameter of the riser pipe.

warnings.intake_below_well_bottom: The intake is deeper than the well.
warnings.intake_in_screen: The intake sits inside a screen interval.
warnings.multiple_open_installations: More than one installation has no removal date.
warnings.removed_before_installed: The removal date must be after the installation date.

meter.title: Meters
meter.intro: One entry per installation of a totalizer (water meter). Device facts only: every register value, including the installation and removal readings, is a reading in Production.
meter.deleteConfirmWithReadings: This meter has readings in the production ledger. They stay in the file but will no longer resolve to a meter. Delete it anyway?
meter.readingsInfo: Record the register values at installation and removal as meter readings in Production, dated at these instants.

fields.serialInfo: A meter removed and reinstalled gets a new entry with the same serial number.
fields.removedAtInfo: Leave empty while the meter is installed.
fields.maxReadingInfo: Largest value the register shows before rolling over to zero. Used to derive the volume across a rollover.

regime.title: Operating regime
regime.intro: How the well is intended to run from a given moment. A change of regime is a new entry; the latest one already in effect is the regime in force. A stopped well is a status change in the history log, not a zero flow.
regime.unknownInfo: Leave a field empty when it is unknown — an empty field never means zero.

fields.effectiveFromInfo: Unique within the block. There is no end date: the next regime replaces this one.

production.title: Production
production.intro: Append-only ledger of water produced: meter readings and declared volumes. Entries are never edited — a correction is a new entry that retracts the original.
production.correctInfo: The correction is saved as a new entry that retracts this one. The original stays in the file but no longer counts.
production.deleteInfo: Deleting removes the entry from the file. To fix a wrong value, prefer a correction, which keeps the history. Delete anyway?
production.noMeters: Add a meter first to record its readings.

fields.readingInfo: Register value. Choose the volume unit in Settings to enter readings of meters that count in liters or gallons — they are stored in m³.
fields.methodInfo: Estimated volumes count only where no meter reading covers the period. Reported volumes (as declared to a regulator) are kept for comparison and never added to the total.

totals.totalInfo: Metered plus estimated volumes. Meters take precedence over estimates.
totals.reportedInfo: Volumes declared to a regulator, for comparison only.

production.unknownIntervals: {n} interval between readings has an unknown volume (the register went down and the meter has no register capacity). | {n} intervals between readings have an unknown volume (the register went down and the meter has no register capacity).
production.noPeriods: No volume can be derived yet.
production.retractedInfo: A later entry corrects this one. It stays in the file but no longer counts.
production.correctionInfo: This entry corrects an earlier one.

wellStatus.title: Well status
wellStatus.unknownInfo: The status is derived from “Status change” entries in the history log. None has been recorded yet.
wellStatus.derivedInfo: Derived from the latest “Status change” entry in the history log.

permit.title: Permits
permit.intro: One entry per legal instrument. The attached document is authoritative. A renewal is a new permit that supersedes the previous one; status and condition deadlines are derived.

fields.typeInfo: A renewal is not a type: create a new permit of the same type that supersedes the previous one.
fields.numberInfo: Portaria or process number, as written in the document.
fields.validFromInfo: Leave empty when valid from the issue date.
fields.validUntilInfo: Leave empty when there is no fixed expiry.
fields.renewalRequestedAtInfo: A renewal filed on or before the expiry keeps the permit active while it is pending.
fields.volumeLimitsInfo: Only volumes stated in the document. Volumes implied by flow × time are derived, never stored.
fields.monthlyScheduleInfo: When a schedule exists, months left empty have no abstraction granted.
fields.supersedesInfo: The permit this one legally replaces (renewal).

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.descriptionInfo: Text of the condition as written in the document.
conditions.noStartDate: Needs an issue or start date to resolve.
conditions.undoConfirm: Remove this fulfillment from the history log?

fulfill.title: Condition fulfilled
fulfill.info: Recorded as a history log entry. Attach the proof of submission as condition evidence.

warnings.valid_until_before_valid_from: The expiry date is before the start date.
warnings.supersedes_unresolved: The superseded permit does not exist in this file.
warnings.supersedes_cycle: The supersedes chain loops back on itself.
warnings.overlapping_validity: Another permit of the same type overlaps this one.
warnings.daily_operating_time_out_of_range: A daily operating time is outside 0–24 h.
warnings.monthly_above_max: A monthly value is above the permit maximum.
warnings.duplicate_month: A month appears more than once in the schedule.
warnings.duplicate_volume_period: A volume period appears more than once.
warnings.duplicate_condition_id: Two conditions share the same id.
warnings.condition_due_conflict: A condition has both a fixed date and a relative deadline; the fixed date wins.
warnings.invalid_duration: A condition has an invalid duration.
warnings.unmatched_condition_log: A fulfillment in the history log matches no deadline of this permit.

warnings.meter_removed_before_installed: The removal date must be after the installation date.
warnings.overlapping_meters: This meter is installed at the same time as another one.
warnings.duplicate_meter_id: Two meters share the same id.
warnings.reading_meter_unresolved: The meter of this reading does not exist in this file.
warnings.reading_outside_installation: This reading is outside the meter installation period.
warnings.reading_rollover_unknown: The register went down and the meter has no register capacity: the volume of this interval is unknown.
warnings.duplicate_production_id: Two production entries share the same id.
warnings.corrects_unresolved: The corrected entry does not exist in this file.
warnings.corrects_cycle: The correction chain loops back on itself.
warnings.declared_period_invalid: The period end must be after its start.
warnings.estimated_overlaps_meter: This estimated volume overlaps meter readings; the meter takes precedence.
warnings.duplicate_regime_id: Two regimes share the same id.
warnings.regime_duplicate_effective_from: Another regime starts at the same instant.
warnings.regime_exceeds_permit: The regime in force is above the flow or daily operation granted by the active permit.
warnings.log_category_field_mismatch: This entry has fields that belong to another category.
warnings.log_reference_unresolved: A referenced pump, meter or event does not exist in this file.
warnings.log_after_decommission: This entry is dated after the well was decommissioned or abandoned.
warnings.missing_maintenance_type: This maintenance entry references data but has no maintenance type.
warnings.missing_status: This status change has no status.
warnings.analysis_uses_retracted_event: This analysis uses an event that has been retracted.

units.title: Customizable units
units.body: You can switch length (m/ft) and diameter (mm/in) units in Settings.
